142: ## Phase 0.4: security & isolation
143: 
144: `security-isolation.js` asserts the fail-closed security and
145: concurrency-isolation contract against the same configurable
146: production-component URL:
147: 
148: - **S1** — wrong-issuer token fails closed (401 + public `WWW-Authenticate`);
149: - **S2** — wrong-audience token fails closed (401 + public `WWW-Authenticate`);
150: - **S3** — wrong-signature token fails closed (401 + public `WWW-Authenticate`);
151: - **S4** — expired token fails closed (401 + public `WWW-Authenticate`);
152: - **S5** — wrong-client token fails closed (401 + public `WWW-Authenticate`);
153: - **S6** — missing grant denies `calendar_list` without disclosing calendars;
154: - **S7** — revoked grant denies `calendar_list` without disclosing calendars;
155: - **S8** — broadened grant does not disclose unauthorized calendars;
156: - **S9** — two concurrent authenticated clients cannot observe each other's
157:   identity, calendars, session, or grant state.
158: 
159: Baseline expectation (Phase 0.4): against the **current** production component,
160: S1-S9 **fail** because the authorization service is not deployed and the MCP
161: gateway does not implement token validation, grant enforcement, or concurrency
162: isolation. The harness therefore **exits non-zero** against the current
163: production component — the intentional, asserted exit condition for this phase
164: and the regression gate for later phases.

167: node mcp-acceptance/security-isolation.js

169: MCP_URL=https://staging.example.com/mcp \
170: MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER=https://auth.staging.example.com \
171:   node mcp-acceptance/security-isolation.js
172: ```
173: 
174: | Variable             | Default                          | Description                              |
175: | -------------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
176: | `MCP_URL`            | `https://mcal.hajnal.space/mcp`  | The MCP endpoint URL to probe.           |
177: | `MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER`   | `https://cal.hajnal.space`       | The configured authorization-server issuer. |
178: | `MCP_REDIRECT`       | `http://127.0.0.1:8765/callback` | The admitted loopback redirect URI.      |
179: | `MCP_TIMEOUT_MS`     | `15000`                          | Request timeout in milliseconds.         |
180: | `MCP_RECORD_DIR`     | OS temp directory                | Where the deterministic record is written. |
181: 
182: Exit codes: `0` all assertions pass; `1` one or more assertions fail (the
183: intentional Phase 0.4 baseline against the current production component);
184: `2` harness error. The deterministic record is written to
185: `$MCP_RECORD_DIR/mcp-acceptance-security-isolation.json`.
186: 
187: ## Requirements
188: 
189: - Node.js 18 or newer (global `fetch`). CI uses Node 22.
190: - No third-party dependencies. The harness uses only Node built-ins.
191: 
192: ## Invocation
193: 
194: Run the focused command from the repository root:
195: 
196: ```sh
197: node mcp-acceptance/harness.js
198: ```
199: 
200: By default this targets the production endpoint
201: (`https://mcal.hajnal.space/mcp`). To target a production-equivalent deployment
202: or a local instance, set `MCP_URL`:
203: 
204: ```sh
205: # Target a production-equivalent deployment (e.g. a staging ingress)
206: MCP_URL=https://staging.example.com/mcp node mcp-acceptance/harness.js
207: 
208: # Target a locally running production component (same mcp-server binary)
209: MCP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3001/mcp node mcp-acceptance/harness.js
210: ```
211: 
212: ### Configuration (environment variables)
213: 
214: | Variable               | Default                          | Description                                  |
215: | ---------------------- | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
216: | `MCP_URL`              | `https://mcal.hajnal.space/mcp`  | The MCP endpoint URL to probe.               |
217: | `MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION` | `2025-03-26`                     | The `protocolVersion` to negotiate.          |
218: | `MCP_CLIENT_NAME`      | `commoncal-mcp-acceptance`       | `clientInfo.name` in the initialize request. |
219: | `MCP_CLIENT_VERSION`   | `0.1.0`                          | `clientInfo.version` in the initialize req.  |
220: | `MCP_TIMEOUT_MS`       | `15000`                          | Request timeout in milliseconds.             |
221: | `MCP_RECORD_DIR`       | OS temp directory                | Where the deterministic response record is written. |
222: 
223: ### Exit codes
224: 
225: | Code | Meaning                                                        |
226: | ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
227: | `0`  | `initialize` is standards-compatible (PASS).                   |
228: | `1`  | `initialize` is NOT standards-compatible (FAIL) — the intentional Phase 0.1 baseline exit condition against the current production component. |
229: | `2`  | Harness error (invalid configuration, network failure, unexpected error). |
230: 
231: ### Deterministic record
232: 
233: The harness writes a deterministic record of the request and response (object
234: keys sorted, volatile headers dropped) to
235: `$MCP_RECORD_DIR/mcp-acceptance-initialize.json` (default: the OS temp
236: directory). The path is printed on every run.
237: 
238: ## CI usage
239: 
240: In CI, point the harness at a production-equivalent deployment and treat a
241: non-zero exit as a real failure once the production component is fixed. During
242: Phase 0 the harness is expected to be red; record the failure as the baseline.
243: 
244: ```sh
245: # Example CI step (production-equivalent deployment)
246: MCP_URL=https://staging.example.com/mcp \
247:   MCP_RECORD_DIR="$RUNNER_TEMP/mcp-acceptance" \
248:   node mcp-acceptance/harness.js
249: ```
250: 
251: ## Verification (harness self-test)
252: 
253: A verification-only mock server exercises both the PASS and FAIL paths without
254: touching production. It is not a release artifact.
255: 
256: ```sh
257: # Start the mock server in one terminal
258: node mcp-acceptance/mock/server.js
259: 
260: # In another terminal:
261: # FAIL path — mock mirrors the CURRENT production behavior (expect exit 1)
262: MCP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3999/mcp-current node mcp-acceptance/harness.js
263: echo "exit: $?"   # -> 1
264: 
265: # PASS path — mock returns a standards-compatible initialize (expect exit 0)
266: MCP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3999/mcp-compliant node mcp-acceptance/harness.js
267: echo "exit: $?"   # -> 0
268: ```
269: 
270: Self-contained verifiers (they start and clean up the mock server themselves):
271: 
272: ```sh
273: # Phase 0.1 harness: both exit paths (default mock port 3999)
274: node mcp-acceptance/verify.js
275: 
276: # Phase 0.2 discovery harness: both exit paths with focused A1/A2/A4
277: # violations on the FAIL path and a passing A3 (default mock port 3998,
278: # issuer host 3999; use --port to avoid collisions)
279: node mcp-acceptance/verify-discovery.js
280: 
281: # Phase 0.3 oauth-lifecycle harness: both exit paths (default mock port 4001,
282: # issuer host 4002; use --port to avoid collisions)
283: node mcp-acceptance/verify-oauth-lifecycle.js
284: 
285: # Phase 0.4 security-isolation harness: both exit paths (default mock port
286: # 4003, issuer host 4004; use --port to avoid collisions)
287: node mcp-acceptance/verify-security-isolation.js
288: ```
289: 
290: The Phase 0.1/0.2 mock (`mock/server.js`) mirrors production's two-host
291: topology: the MCP host (MOCK_PORT) serves the MCP endpoint and the
292: protected-resource metadata; the issuer host (MOCK_ISSUER_PORT, default
293: MOCK_PORT + 1) serves the authorization-server metadata (SPA HTML in the

295: 
296: The Phase 0.3/0.4 mock (`mock/lifecycle-server.js`) is driven by a single

298: production today). In the compliant world it implements the full OAuth + MCP

300: authenticated MCP lifecycle) plus verification-only test hooks (`/_test/*`)
301: for driving the negative token and grant-state cases. In the current world it
302: mirrors the verified current production state (the authorization service is
303: not deployed; the MCP gateway does not implement the MCP lifecycle).

asserted exit condition for this phase and the regression gate for later
phases.

## Phase 0.3: OAuth lifecycle

`oauth-lifecycle.js` asserts the full OAuth + MCP lifecycle against the same
configurable production-component URL:

- **L1** — DCR (RFC 7591) registration succeeds with the supported OpenCode
  loopback redirect shape (201, `client_id` present, no `client_secret`);
- **L2** — Authorization Code flow with `state` and S256 PKCE completes (code
  present, state round-trips);
- **L3** — token exchange completes and yields a resource-bound access token
  (3-part JWT) without manual JWT construction;
- **L4** — with that token, `initialize` succeeds (200, `protocolVersion`,
  `capabilities`, `serverInfo`);
- **L5** — `notifications/initialized` is accepted (202);
- **L6** — `tools/list` returns the expected nine tools, each with a
  description and a complete input schema;
- **L7** — `tools/call calendar_list` succeeds (200, content block).

Baseline expectation (Phase 0.3): against the **current** production component,
L1-L7 **fail** because the authorization service is not deployed (the
advertised issuer host falls through to the CommonCal SPA) and the MCP gateway
does not implement the MCP lifecycle. The harness therefore **exits non-zero**
against the current production component — the intentional, asserted exit
condition for this phase and the regression gate for later phases.

```sh

# or, for a production-equivalent deployment:
MCP_URL=https://staging.example.com/mcp \
MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER=https://auth.staging.example.com \
  node mcp-acceptance/oauth-lifecycle.js
```

| -------------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `MCP_URL`            | `https://mcal.hajnal.space/mcp`  | The MCP endpoint URL to probe.           |
| `MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER`   | `https://cal.hajnal.space`       | The configured authorization-server issuer. |
| `MCP_REDIRECT`       | `http://127.0.0.1:8765/callback` | The admitted loopback redirect URI.      |
| `MCP_TIMEOUT_MS`     | `15000`                          | Request timeout in milliseconds.         |
| `MCP_RECORD_DIR`     | OS temp directory                | Where the deterministic record is written. |

Exit codes: `0` all assertions pass; `1` one or more assertions fail (the
intentional Phase 0.3 baseline against the current production component);
`2` harness error. The deterministic record is written to
`$MCP_RECORD_DIR/mcp-acceptance-oauth-lifecycle.json`.

## Phase 0.4: security & isolation

`security-isolation.js` asserts the fail-closed security and
concurrency-isolation contract against the same configurable
production-component URL:

- **S1** — wrong-issuer token fails closed (401 + public `WWW-Authenticate`);
- **S2** — wrong-audience token fails closed (401 + public `WWW-Authenticate`);
- **S3** — wrong-signature token fails closed (401 + public `WWW-Authenticate`);
- **S4** — expired token fails closed (401 + public `WWW-Authenticate`);
- **S5** — wrong-client token fails closed (401 + public `WWW-Authenticate`);
- **S6** — missing grant denies `calendar_list` without disclosing calendars;
- **S7** — revoked grant denies `calendar_list` without disclosing calendars;
- **S8** — broadened grant does not disclose unauthorized calendars;
- **S9** — two concurrent authenticated clients cannot observe each other's
  identity, calendars, session, or grant state.

Baseline expectation (Phase 0.4): against the **current** production component,
S1-S9 **fail** because the authorization service is not deployed and the MCP
gateway does not implement token validation, grant enforcement, or concurrency
isolation. The harness therefore **exits non-zero** against the current
production component — the intentional, asserted exit condition for this phase
and the regression gate for later phases.

```sh

# or, for a production-equivalent deployment:
MCP_URL=https://staging.example.com/mcp \
MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER=https://auth.staging.example.com \
  node mcp-acceptance/security-isolation.js
```

| -------------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `MCP_URL`            | `https://mcal.hajnal.space/mcp`  | The MCP endpoint URL to probe.           |
| `MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER`   | `https://cal.hajnal.space`       | The configured authorization-server issuer. |
| `MCP_REDIRECT`       | `http://127.0.0.1:8765/callback` | The admitted loopback redirect URI.      |
| `MCP_TIMEOUT_MS`     | `15000`                          | Request timeout in milliseconds.         |
| `MCP_RECORD_DIR`     | OS temp directory                | Where the deterministic record is written. |

Exit codes: `0` all assertions pass; `1` one or more assertions fail (the
intentional Phase 0.4 baseline against the current production component);
`2` harness error. The deterministic record is written to
`$MCP_RECORD_DIR/mcp-acceptance-security-isolation.json`.

## Requirements

- Node.js 18 or newer (global `fetch`). CI uses Node 22.
- No third-party dependencies. The harness uses only Node built-ins.

## Invocation

Run the focused command from the repository root:

```sh
node mcp-acceptance/harness.js
```

By default this targets the production endpoint
(`https://mcal.hajnal.space/mcp`). To target a production-equivalent deployment
or a local instance, set `MCP_URL`:

```sh
# Target a production-equivalent deployment (e.g. a staging ingress)
MCP_URL=https://staging.example.com/mcp node mcp-acceptance/harness.js

# Target a locally running production component (same mcp-server binary)
MCP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3001/mcp node mcp-acceptance/harness.js
```

### Configuration (environment variables)

| Variable               | Default                          | Description                                  |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `MCP_URL`              | `https://mcal.hajnal.space/mcp`  | The MCP endpoint URL to probe.               |
| `MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION` | `2025-03-26`                     | The `protocolVersion` to negotiate.          |
| `MCP_CLIENT_NAME`      | `commoncal-mcp-acceptance`       | `clientInfo.name` in the initialize request. |
| `MCP_CLIENT_VERSION`   | `0.1.0`                          | `clientInfo.version` in the initialize req.  |
| `MCP_TIMEOUT_MS`       | `15000`                          | Request timeout in milliseconds.             |
| `MCP_RECORD_DIR`       | OS temp directory                | Where the deterministic response record is written. |

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning                                                        |
| ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `0`  | `initialize` is standards-compatible (PASS).                   |
| `1`  | `initialize` is NOT standards-compatible (FAIL) — the intentional Phase 0.1 baseline exit condition against the current production component. |
| `2`  | Harness error (invalid configuration, network failure, unexpected error). |

### Deterministic record

The harness writes a deterministic record of the request and response (object
keys sorted, volatile headers dropped) to
`$MCP_RECORD_DIR/mcp-acceptance-initialize.json` (default: the OS temp
directory). The path is printed on every run.

## CI usage

In CI, point the harness at a production-equivalent deployment and treat a
non-zero exit as a real failure once the production component is fixed. During
Phase 0 the harness is expected to be red; record the failure as the baseline.

```sh
# Example CI step (production-equivalent deployment)
MCP_URL=https://staging.example.com/mcp \
  MCP_RECORD_DIR="$RUNNER_TEMP/mcp-acceptance" \
  node mcp-acceptance/harness.js
```

## Verification (harness self-test)

A verification-only mock server exercises both the PASS and FAIL paths without
touching production. It is not a release artifact.

```sh
# Start the mock server in one terminal
node mcp-acceptance/mock/server.js

# In another terminal:
# FAIL path — mock mirrors the CURRENT production behavior (expect exit 1)
MCP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3999/mcp-current node mcp-acceptance/harness.js
echo "exit: $?"   # -> 1

# PASS path — mock returns a standards-compatible initialize (expect exit 0)
MCP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3999/mcp-compliant node mcp-acceptance/harness.js
echo "exit: $?"   # -> 0
```

Self-contained verifiers (they start and clean up the mock server themselves):

```sh
# Phase 0.1 harness: both exit paths (default mock port 3999)
node mcp-acceptance/verify.js

# Phase 0.2 discovery harness: both exit paths with focused A1/A2/A4
# violations on the FAIL path and a passing A3 (default mock port 3998,
# issuer host 3999; use --port to avoid collisions)
node mcp-acceptance/verify-discovery.js

# Phase 0.3 oauth-lifecycle harness: both exit paths (default mock port 4001,
# issuer host 4002; use --port to avoid collisions)
node mcp-acceptance/verify-oauth-lifecycle.js

# Phase 0.4 security-isolation harness: both exit paths (default mock port
# 4003, issuer host 4004; use --port to avoid collisions)
node mcp-acceptance/verify-security-isolation.js
```

The Phase 0.1/0.2 mock (`mock/server.js`) mirrors production's two-host
topology: the MCP host (MOCK_PORT) serves the MCP endpoint and the
protected-resource metadata; the issuer host (MOCK_ISSUER_PORT, default
MOCK_PORT + 1) serves the authorization-server metadata (SPA HTML in the
current mode, valid JSON in the compliant mode).

The Phase 0.3/0.4 mock (`mock/lifecycle-server.js`) is driven by a single
world selector (`MOCK_WORLD`, default `compliant`; `current` mirrors
production today). In the compliant world it implements the full OAuth + MCP
lifecycle (DCR, Authorization Code + S256 PKCE, token exchange, JWKS, and the
authenticated MCP lifecycle) plus verification-only test hooks (`/_test/*`)
for driving the negative token and grant-state cases. In the current world it
mirrors the verified current production state (the authorization service is
not deployed; the MCP gateway does not implement the MCP lifecycle).

## Files

- `harness.js` — the Phase 0.1 standalone black-box harness (initialize
  standards-compliance).
- `discovery.js` — the Phase 0.2 standalone black-box harness (public 401
  challenge + protected-resource and authorization-server metadata discovery).
- `oauth-lifecycle.js` — the Phase 0.3 standalone black-box harness (DCR,
  Authorization Code + S256 PKCE, token exchange, and the authenticated MCP
  lifecycle through `calendar_list`).
- `security-isolation.js` — the Phase 0.4 standalone black-box harness
  (fail-closed token/grant cases and concurrent-identity isolation).
- `lib.js` — shared helpers for the Phase 0.3/0.4 harnesses (OAuth flow, MCP
  calls, JWT helpers, deterministic JSON).
- `fixtures/initialize-request.json` — the `initialize` request fixture (reused
  from the slice1-lab request shape; owned by this harness).
- `verify.js` — self-contained verification of both Phase 0.1 harness exit
  paths.
- `verify-discovery.js` — self-contained verification of both Phase 0.2
  harness exit paths, including the focused A1/A2/A4 violations and the
  passing A3 on the FAIL path.
- `verify-oauth-lifecycle.js` — self-contained verification of both Phase 0.3
  harness exit paths.
- `verify-security-isolation.js` — self-contained verification of both Phase
  0.4 harness exit paths.
- `mock/server.js` — verification-only mock server for Phase 0.1/0.2 (PASS +
  FAIL fixtures, two-host topology).
- `mock/lifecycle-server.js` — verification-only mock server for Phase 0.3/0.4
  (full OAuth + MCP lifecycle, world selector, test hooks).
- `mock/oauth-provider.js` — verification-only mock OAuth provider (DCR,
  Authorization Code + S256 PKCE, token exchange, JWKS, token validation,
  grants, token minting).
- `README.md` — this document.

320:       `HTTP status is ${resp.status}; a standards-compatible initialize must return 200`
321:     );
322:   }
323: 
324:   if (resp.bodyJsonParseError !== null) {
325:     violations.push(
326:       `response body is not valid JSON: ${resp.bodyJsonParseError}`
327:     );
328:     return violations;
329:   }
330: 
331:   if (!isPlainObject(body)) {
332:     violations.push("response body is not a JSON object");
333:     return violations;
334:   }
335: 
336:   if (body.jsonrpc !== "2.0") {
337:     violations.push(
338:       `jsonrpc is ${JSON.stringify(body.jsonrpc)}; expected "2.0"`
339:     );
340:   }
341: 
342:   if (body.id !== record.request.id) {
343:     violations.push(
344:       `response id is ${JSON.stringify(body.id)}; expected ${JSON.stringify(record.request.id)}`
345:     );
346:   }
347: 
348:   if (body.error !== undefined) {
349:     const e = body.error;
350:     const code = isPlainObject(e) && e.code !== undefined ? e.code : "?";
351:     const message = isPlainObject(e) && e.message ? e.message : "(no message)";
352:     violations.push(`response contains JSON-RPC error ${code}: ${message}`);
353:   }
354: 
355:   if (body.result === undefined) {
356:     violations.push("response has no 'result' member");
357:     return violations;
358:   }
359: 
360:   const result = body.result;
361:   if (!isPlainObject(result)) {
362:     violations.push("'result' is not an object");
363:     return violations;
364:   }
365: 
366:   if (typeof result.protocolVersion !== "string") {
367:     violations.push("result.protocolVersion is missing or not a string");
368:   }
369: 
370:   if (!isPlainObject(result.capabilities)) {
371:     violations.push("result.capabilities is missing or not an object");
372:   }
373: 
374:   const serverInfo = result.serverInfo;
375:   if (!isPlainObject(serverInfo)) {
376:     violations.push("result.serverInfo is missing or not an object");
377:   } else {
378:     if (typeof serverInfo.name !== "string") {
379:       violations.push("result.serverInfo.name is missing or not a string");
380:     }
381:     if (typeof serverInfo.version !== "string") {
382:       violations.push("result.serverInfo.version is missing or not a string");
383:     }
384:   }
385: 
386:   return violations;
387: }
388: 
389: /**
390:  * Serialize a value to deterministic JSON (object keys sorted recursively).
391:  */
392: function deterministicStringify(value) {
393:   function sort(value) {
394:     if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map(sort);
395:     if (isPlainObject(value)) {
396:       const out = {};
397:       for (const key of Object.keys(value).sort()) {
398:         out[key] = sort(value[key]);
399:       }
400:       return out;
401:     }
402:     return value;
403:   }
404:   return JSON.stringify(sort(value), null, 2);
405: }
406: 
407: function writeRecord(cfg, record) {
408:   fs.mkdirSync(cfg.recordDir, { recursive: true });
409:   const recordPath = path.join(cfg.recordDir, "mcp-acceptance-initialize.json");
410:   const envelope = {
411:     harness: HARNESS_NAME,
412:     harnessVersion: HARNESS_VERSION,
413:     target: cfg.url,
414:     recordedBy: "baseline-initialize-probe",
415:     record,
416:   };
417:   fs.writeFileSync(recordPath, deterministicStringify(envelope) + "\n", "utf8");
418:   return recordPath;
419: }
420: 
421: async function main() {
422:   const flags = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2));
423: 
424:   if (flags.help) {
425:     printHelp();
426:     return 0;
427:   }
428: 
429:   if (flags._unknown.length > 0) {
430:     console.error(
431:       `[mcp-acceptance] CONFIG ERROR: unknown argument(s): ${flags._unknown.join(", ")}`
432:     );
433:     console.error("[mcp-acceptance] Run with --help for usage.");
434:     return 2;
435:   }
436: 
437:   let cfg;
438:   try {
439:     cfg = loadConfig(flags);
440:   } catch (err) {
441:     if (err instanceof HarnessError) {
442:       console.error(`[mcp-acceptance] CONFIG ERROR: ${err.message}`);
443:       return 2;
444:     }
445:     throw err;
446:   }
447: 
448:   console.log(`[mcp-acceptance] target: ${cfg.url}`);
449:   console.log(`[mcp-acceptance] protocolVersion: ${cfg.protocolVersion}`);
450: 
451:   let record;
452:   try {
453:     record = await probeInitialize(cfg);
454:   } catch (err) {
455:     if (err instanceof HarnessError) {
456:       console.error(`[mcp-acceptance] PROBE ERROR: ${err.message}`);
457:       return 2;
458:     }
459:     throw err;
460:   }
461: 
462:   const violations = validateInitialize(record);
463:   let recordPath = null;
464:   try {
465:     recordPath = writeRecord(cfg, record);
466:   } catch (err) {
467:     // Recording is best-effort; a failure to write the record must not mask the
468:     // actual standards-compliance result.
469:     console.error(
470:       `[mcp-acceptance] WARNING: could not write record: ${describeError(err)}`
471:     );
472:   }
473: 
474:   const resp = record.response;
475:   console.log(`[mcp-acceptance] response status: ${resp.status}`);
476:   if (resp.bodyJsonParseError !== null) {
477:     console.log(`[mcp-acceptance] response body (non-JSON): ${resp.bodyRaw}`);
478:   } else if (isPlainObject(resp.bodyJson)) {
479:     console.log(
480:       `[mcp-acceptance] response body: ${deterministicStringify(resp.bodyJson)}`
481:     );
482:   } else {
483:     console.log(`[mcp-acceptance] response body: ${resp.bodyRaw}`);
484:   }
485: 
486:   if (violations.length > 0) {
487:     console.log("");
488:     console.log(
489:       "[mcp-acceptance] FAIL: initialize is NOT standards-compatible"
490:     );
491:     for (const v of violations) {
492:       console.log(`  - ${v}`);
493:     }
494:     if (recordPath) {
495:       console.log(`[mcp-acceptance] deterministic record: ${recordPath}`);
496:     }
497:     console.log("");

500:     );
501:     console.log(

503:     );
504:     console.log(

506:     );

512:   if (recordPath) {

 * A standalone black-box harness that targets a configurable production-component

 * configuration, lifecycle, reporting, and cleanup: it is a pure HTTP client,
